subject: in pcountOpen, using obsCovs to estimate lambda, gamma, or omega?

messages.author: 61f41542e631370b
messages.subject: in pcountOpen, using obsCovs to estimate lambda, gamma, or omega?
parts:
Is it possible to use obsCovs to estimate lambda, gamma, or omega? For example, I have been playing with the alfl0506 data and pcountOpen script from the January Webinar. When I try to include time as a covariate to help estimate lambda like this:

 

(fm5 <- pcountOpen(~time, ~1, ~1, ~1, alfl.umf, K=30))

 

I get this error:

in model.frame.default(lamformula, siteCovs, na.action = NULL) :

  object is not a matrix

 

The reason I ask is that I am hoping to use monthly fruiting of tree species in three different sites as covariates to explain monthly bird counts. I don't think I can include fruiting as siteCovs because fruiting is not a constant feature of my sites – it changes each month.

 

I have attached an example spreadsheet showing how I think I would need to setup my data to use pcountOpen.  Though I've only included 6 dates, I have 18 dates in my full data set. I welcome any suggestions.

 

Thanks, Rhine

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] in pcountOpen, using obsCovs to estimate lambda, gamma, or omega?
parts:
Hi Rhine,

For pcountOpen(), "obsCovs" are only used for modeling detection probability when you collected data using the so-called "robust design" (which is always the preferred option). The possible covariate options for the 4 parameters are this:

lambda: siteCovs only
omega/gamma: siteCovs or yearlySiteCovs
p: siteCovs, yearlySiteCovs, or obsCovs (if you have the robust design)


Richard
